newsitem.title: BELGIUM: U.S. renderers see higher 1997 meal prices.
newsitem.headline: U.S. renderers see higher 1997 meal prices.

text.p: United States animal meal prices should rise in 1997 after firm levels were achieved in 1996, said Bruce Blanton, the executive director of the National Renderers Association

He told the Lipidex 97 oilseeds conference here the $2.5 billion industry that turns animal remains into animal foodstuff ingredients increased its 1996 profits amid high fat and proteins prices and strong domestic demand.
But there were two wild cards this year in the wake of the European crisis over bovine spongifom encephalopathy (BSE).

The Food and Drug Administration had proposed to ban the use of protein from ruminants in feed for those animals as British evidence suggests an association between BSE cases, of which there are none in the U.S., and this feeding practice.

The other is the so-called cosmetic directive which will potentially affect the exports of U.S. tallow to Europe, where legislators seek to restrict the use of animal products in areas possibly endangering human health.
Blanton said the industry hoped crop weather damage to corn and soybeans may boost oilmeal and feedgrain prices and in turn lift animal-derived feeds.
Blanton also said independent analysts had forecast average U.S. manufacturers prices this year as follows (with 1996 averages in brackets) --
Renderer tallow 20-23 cents/lb (20.53 cents), yellow grease 18-21 cents (16), meat/bone meal $280-320/tonne ($242.05), blood meal 50 percent protein $550-600 (478.72).
